newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian vice president readies resignation.
newsitem.headline: Colombian vice president readies resignation.

text.p: Colombian Vice President Humberto de la Calle, a thorn in the side of President Ernesto Samper, will tender his resignation on Tuesday, his aides said on Monday.

They said De la Calle, who urged Samper to step down in an open letter last week, would formally hand in his resignation to the Senate early on Tuesday and then meet the press to discuss the reasons he was leaving the government.

"There will be a news conference at about midday," De la Calle's spokesowman said, adding that was definitely preparing to announce his break with the government and the man to whom he once was second in line.

De la Calle argued in his letter last week that Samper had been severely weakened by a long-running scandal over charges he used drug money to finance his campaign and had lost all effective capacity to lead a nation torn by seemingly uncontrolled levels of violence and general mayhem.
A dangerous power vacuum had led to a situation in which Colombia was literally "falling to pieces," he said.
"The government you preside over is at its worst hour in terms of credibility, legitimacy and capacity to act," De la Calle said in his letter.

Samper, who has endured repeated calls for his resignation because of his alleged ties to drug lords, responded to last Thursday's request from De la Calle by saying he had no intention of leaving office.
He also said it was the vice president who should step down if he insisted on airing his differences with the embattled president in public.

If his resignation is accepted by the Senate, and there seems little doubt that it will be, Congress will then be required to choose a replacement to see out the remaining two years of De la Calle's term.
